newsitem.title: THAILAND: Rising Thai fragrant rice prices upset exporters.
newsitem.headline: Rising Thai fragrant rice prices upset exporters.

text.p: Thai exporters may not be able to meet fragrant rice export commitments because of rising prices, industry sources said.
Thai fragrant rice, considered a premium grade, was quoted at around US$600 per tonne FOB Bangkok compared with $585 last week and an average of $528 in August.

"There is not much fragrant rice left in the stock. And the bad news is the outstanding orders are more than 100,000 tonnes," said Somsuk Srisatetwatana, a board member of Thai Rice Expoters Association.
Besides supply problems, extraordinarily high local and regional demand had also pushed prices up, he told Reuters.
One trader said exporters risked losing up to $40-50 a tonne if they bought the rice from the open market to cover orders.

Most fragrant rice comes from the northeastern region. Market sources said the exact size of stocks was not known but surveys in several major fragrant rice producing provinces showed combined stocks were under 300,000 tonnes.
Rice millers said they did not have much fragrant rice left in their stock either.

"It was actively bought in the past months. Many millers have not bought much rice recently as they have to clear their silos in preparation for floods," said Apichart Amatayakul, the manager of Thai Rice Mills Association.
"Fresh supply will be available by November," he said.
While prices of fragrant rice were bullish, average grade rice prices were either steady or lower on thin demand as buyers turned to countries like India and Vietnam for cheaper rice.
The price of Thai 100 percent grade B rice was around $50 per tonne above Vietnamese 5 percent rice, trade sources said.
